A 32-year-old woman, 4 weeks postpartum, comes to the clinic reporting hip tightness that occurs
during prolonged sitting. During osteopathic structural examination, the following findings are noted: -
Right-sided positive seated flexion test - Anterior motion detected when applying anterior force on the
sacrum in prone position - Deep sacral sulcus on the right side - Posterior inferior lateral angle of the
sacrum noted on the left - L5 vertebra demonstrates left side-bending What is the most accurate
diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Left on right anterior sacral rotation (B) Right on right posterior sacral
torsion (C) Left on left anterior sacral torsion (D) Left sacral shear (E) Bilateral sacral extension
dysfunction (F) Right on left posterior sacral torsion (G) Sacral counternutation dysfunction (H) Right
unilateral sacral flexion (I) Left on left anterior sacral rotation (J) Bilateral sacral flexion dysfunction
 A. Bilateral sacral extension dysfunction
B. Bilateral sacral flexion dysfunction
C. Right unilateral sacral flexion
D. Right on left posterior sacral torsion
E. Left on right anterior sacral rotation
F. Left on left anterior sacral rotation
G. Right on right posterior sacral torsion
H. Left sacral shear
I. Left on left anterior sacral torsion
J. Sacral counternutation dysfunction
